Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 6326 of 2021
Applicant :- Virendra Sonkar And Another

Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Brijesh Kumar Sharma
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Abhai Kumar Singh,Awadhesh Kumar Singh
Hon'ble Mrs. Manju Rani Chauhan,J.
Supplementary Affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicants today in the Court, is taken on record.
Office is directed to register the same.

Heard Mr. Brijesh Kumar Sharma, learned counsel for the applicants and Mr. Pankaj Srivastava,
learned A.G.A and perused the record.
Mr. Lal Bahadur Ram is present in person before the Court.

This anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicants ? Virendra Sonkar and Pramod Kumar Sonkar, seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 391 of 2020, under Sections ?
420, 406 I.P.C., Police Station ? Line Bazar, District - Jaunpur, during the pendency of trial.

Earlier on 22.03.2021, this Court, while granting interim anticipatory bail to the applicants, was passed the following order:-
Virendra Sonkar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142061838/

sentences.text:
"Heard learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Lal Bahadur Ram, informant in person and learned A.G.A for the State.
The instant anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant,
Virendra Sonkar and Pramod Kumar Sonkar, with a prayer to release them on bail in Case Crime No. 391 of 2020, under Sections- 420, 406 I.P.C., Police Station- Line Bazar, District- Jaunpur, during pendency of trial.
Prior notice of this bail application was served in the office of Government Advocate and as per Chapter XVIII, Rule 18 of the Allahabad High Court Rules and as per direction dated 20.11.2020 of this Court in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. 8072 of 2020, Govind Mishra @ Chhotu Versus State of U.P., hence, this anticipatory bail application is being heard.

entities.text: Govind Mishra @ Chhotu Versus State of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Grant of further time to the learned A.G.A as per Section 438 (3) Cr.P.C. (U.P. Amendment) is not required.

There is allegation against the applicants that they have received an amount of Rs.
19,50,000/- in their account from the informant.

Further allegation is that Rs.
1,40,000/- was paid to the applicants in cash also.
Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that no money was received by them in cash and the applicants are willing to return Rs. 19,50,000/- to the informant within a period of one month.
Informant, has appeared in person, and is willing to accept the aforesaid amount from the applicants.
List this case as a fresh case on 27.04.2021.

On the next date fixed, the applicants will file an affidavit proving that they have paid the aforesaid amount to the informant through R.T.G.S. in his bank account and produce the affidavit of the same along with supplementary affidavit.

A copy of this order downloaded from the official website of this court shall also be produced before the S.P/S.S.P concerned by the applicants, if the investigation is still in progress, who shall ensure compliance of this order after due verification from official website of this court. "
Thereafter, on 27.7.2022, the applicants were directed to make payment of outstanding dues i.e. Rs. 11,50,000/- to the informant in installments within a period of three months from that date.

As per the schedule prescribed in the said order, first installment of Rupees Four Lakh was to be paid on or before 27.8.2022, whereas date for second of same amount was on or before 27.9.2022 and the last and third one for remaining amount of Rs. 3,50,000/- was asked to be settled on or before 27.10.2022.
Subsequently, on 19.01.2023, this Court was passed the following order:-

"On 27.7.2022 the applicants were directed to make payment of outstanding dues i.e.
Rs. 11,50,000/- to the informant in installments within a period of three months from that date.

As per the schedule prescribed in the said order, first installment of Rupees Four Lakh was to be paid on or before 27.8.2022, whereas date for second of same amount was on or before 27.9.2022 and the last and third one for remaining amount of Rs. 3,50,000/- was asked to be settled on or before 27.10.2022.
Sri Brijesh Kumar Sharma, learned Counsel appears for the applicants and the informant Sri Lal Bahadur Ram is present in-person before the Court.

The informant submits that dubious attitude of the applicants is apparent as they did not make the payment even after passage of about five months since the directions issued by this Court on 27.7.2022 and he has been made to suffer a lot.

sentences.text:
Perusal of the order sheet reveals that the case was listed thrice previously, however,
firstly it got adjourned on 01.11.2022 on the ground of medical condition of the applicants.
On the next date viz. 21.11.2022 next date was fixed as 30.11.2022 at the request of learned counsel for the applicants and on last occasion i.e. 02.1.2023 no one turned up on their behalf.

Learned counsel appearing for the applicants today again seeks further twenty days'
time to comply with the order dated 27.7.2022, however, the informant who is present in-person before this Court raises serious objection and doubt over the applicants' intention.
Since the applicants have enjoyed the liberty sans respect thereto granted by this Court, no sympathetic consideration remains to accord more indulgence over applicants' grievance.

Therefore, following directions are issued:
(i) The entire outstanding amount i.e. Rs. 9,50,000/- be paid to the informant either in single deposit or in installments however within twenty days from today;
( ii) An affidavit to the aforesaid effect be filed before the Court/ authority concerned by the applicants within twenty days from today;
(iii) No interim protection remains survives in the present matter as on previous dates too it was not extended.

(iv) Failure of payment of the outstanding amount within prescribed twenty days'
period will require the Superintendent of Police, Jaunpur to ensure applicants'
presence before this Court.
List this case on 13th February, 2023 peremptorily, for further hearing.

Copy of this order be made available to Sri S.K. Pal, learned Government Advocate, who is present in the Court for communication to the Superintendent of Police, Jaunpur and its compliance Registrar Compliance shall communicate this order to the concerned court as well as authority to proceed in accordance with law and ensure its compliance."
In compliance of the aforesaid order dated 19.01.2023, a compliance affidavit has been placed on record as is evident from the office report dated 20.02.2023.

Learned counsel for the applicants submits that due amount has already been paid to the opposite party no.2 as is evident from the bank statement, which has been annexed as Annexure no.SA-1 to the supplementary affidavit.
However, for the offence, which has been committed, the amount of interest is still to be seen by the Investigating Officer.
The investigation is still pending and the applicant is ready and willing to cooperate in the investigation.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicants to demonstrate the falsity of the allegation made against them.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants undertakes that he has co-operated in the investigation and is ready to do so in trial also failing which the State can move appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail.
Mr. Lal Bahadur Ram, in person, has accepted that he has received the due amount as alleged in the FIR.

After the close scrutiny of Section 438 Cr.P.C. and its relevant clauses, the Court is satisfied that the applicant has made out the case for anticipatory bail in connection with aforesaid case crime pending investigation.

(iv) The Investigating Officer of the case would make all necessary endeavour to gear up the investigation in utmost transparent way and would try to conclude the same before the next date fixed.
The Investigating Officer is directed to conclude the investigation of the present case in accordance with law before the next date fixed independently without being prejudiced by any observation made by this Court while considering and deciding the present anticipatory bail application of the applicants.
In the event, the applicants breach or attempt to breach any of the aforesaid conditions or wilfully violate above conditions or abstains himself from the investigation, it would be open for the Investigating Officer or the concerned authority to apply before the court of Session for cancellation of interim protection and the Court of Session has every liberty and freedom to revoke the anticipatory bail after recording the reasons for the same.

Till then, in case of their arrest, the applicants shall be enlarged on interim anticipatory bail in the aforesaid proceedings on their furnishing personal bonds of Rs. 50,000/- each and two sureties each of like amount before the Station House Officer of Police Station/Court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicants shall make themselves available for interrogation by the police officer as and when required, if investigation is in progress;
(ii) The applicants shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade such person from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;

2 (iii) The applicants shall not leave the country without the previous permission of the Court and if they have passport, the same shall be deposited by them before the S.S.P./S.P. concerned/Court concerned;
(iv) The party shall file computer generated copy of such order downloaded from the official website of High Court Allahabad before the Court/Authority/Official concerned; and (v) The concerned Court/Authority/Official shall verify the authenticity of such computerized copy of the order from the official website of High Court Allahabad and shall make a declaration of such verification in writing.
In default of any of the conditions, the Investigating Officer/Government Advocate is at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of interim anticipatory bail granted to the applicants.
The Investigating Officer will continue with the investigation, if it is in progress and will not be affected by this order.
A copy of this order downloaded from the official website of this court shall also be produced before the S.P/S.S.P concerned by the applicants, if the investigation is still in progress, who shall ensure compliance of this order after due verification from official website of this court. "
Thereafter, on 27.7.2022, the applicants were directed to make payment of outstanding dues i.e. Rs. 11,50,000/- to the informant in installments within a period of three months from that date.
Therefore, following directions are issued:
(i) The entire outstanding amount i.e. Rs. 9,50,000/- be paid to the informant either in single deposit or in installments however within twenty days from today;
( ii) An affidavit to the aforesaid effect be filed before the Court/ authority concerned by the applicants within twenty days from today;
(iv) Failure of payment of the outstanding amount within prescribed twenty days'
period will require the Superintendent of Police, Jaunpur to ensure applicants'
presence before this Court.
Without expressing any opinion upon ultimate merits of the case either ways which may be adversely affect the investigation and subsequent stage of the case, the Court directs that in the event of arrest of the applicants in aforesaid case crime, he shall be released on anticipatory bail on furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer till the submission of police report under section 173(2) Cr.P.C.
by the investigating officer, with the following conditions that :
(i) the applicants shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required;
(ii) the applicants shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police office;
(iii) the applicants shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court and if he has passport the same shall be deposited by him before the S.S.P./S.P.
concerned.
(iv) The Investigating Officer of the case would make all necessary endeavour to gear up the investigation in utmost transparent way and would try to conclude the same before the next date fixed.
The Investigating Officer is directed to conclude the investigation of the present case in accordance with law before the next date fixed independently without being prejudiced by any observation made by this Court while considering and deciding the present anticipatory bail application of the applicants.
In the event, the applicants breach or attempt to breach any of the aforesaid conditions or wilfully violate above conditions or abstains himself from the investigation, it would be open for the Investigating Officer or the concerned authority to apply before the court of Session for cancellation of interim protection and the Court of Session has every liberty and freedom to revoke the anticipatory bail after recording the reasons for the same.

Accordingly, this anticipatory bail application U/s Section 438 Cr.P.C. is disposed off.
